newsitem.title: JAPAN: Traders say N.Korea grain deal defunct.
newsitem.headline: Traders say N.Korea grain deal defunct.

text.p: Asian grain industry sources said on Thursday they understood that a zinc-for-wheat barter deal between North Korea and Cargill Inc had been called off, despite a claim from Pyongyang that talks were continuing.
The sources said the U.S. grains giant had already sold the 20,000-tonne shipment of wheat that had originally been destined for North Korea to other buyers in Southeast Asia.
Cash-strapped North Korea, hit by famine, needs massive imports to feed its 23 million population. Severe floods destroyed food stocks and grain harvests in North Korea in 1995 and 1996.
International aid agencies have warned that tens of thousands of people could starve to death in North Korea over the next few months unless it receives substantial food imports.
Late on Wednesday, North Korea denied it had called off the barter agreement and accused Cargill of spreading "groundless rumours".

Pyongyang said the deal was still under discussion and that North Korea had not unilaterally pulled out, as Cargill had said. The comments by a North Korean trade official were carried by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).
A spokesman for Cargill Japan Ltd said the company could not immediately comment on the matter.
The barter deal, finalised in early April, called for the U.S. grains giant to swap 20,000 tonnes of wheat for 4,000 tonnes of North Korean zinc.

Cargill said earlier this month that North Korea had cancelled the deal without explanation and that no further discussions on a barter deal were envisaged, although the firm said it remained interested in commercial sales to Pyongyang.
"We're informed that Cargill already sold the wheat to other buyers in Southeast Asia, not to North Korea," an official at a major trade house in Tokyo said.
Pyongyang and the U.S. grains trade house are no longer in talks on the barter deal, said one source in the Asian grain trade.
